episodes.154248: Training convection ahead of a cold front resulted in bands of heavy rain in a short period of time and a couple of reports of flash flooding.  The heaviest amounts of 5 to 8 inches fell in a swath from Franklin county northeastward to Jefferson county.
episodes.154652: A stalled front stretched from the northeastern Gulf into the Florida Big Bend into southern Georgia with a band of moderate to briefly heavy showers mainly over interior southeast Georgia. An upper level low over the northern Gulf invigorated convection lifting shortwave energy from the Gulf of Mexico along the frontal boundary which increased rainfall intensity. A Flash Flood Watch was in effect for portions of SE Georgia.
episodes.155516: Heavy rain brought flooding to the Ouachita, White, and Cache rivers.
episodes.164555: From December 29 - January 16, a strong and persistent Aleutian Low pressure system developed in the eastern Pacific which directed the jet stream and primary storm track at Washington State that resulted in a rapid series of atmospheric rivers and wind storms that battered Washington State. Water vapor transport into Washington State averaged 160-200% of normal during the period from December 29 through January 16. Numerous periods of heavy rain occurred during the episode, which in turn resulted in widespread and sustained river flooding, urban and small stream flooding, mudslides, and landslides in addition to the significant and widespread impacts from high winds, pounding surf, and coastal flooding.||During the wettest portion of this 19-day period, Washington State experienced widespread precipitation totals between 200% and 350% of normal. The prolonged bouts of moderate to heavy rain between December 29, 2020 and January 7, 2021, resulted in 8 major rivers exceeding flood stage; with 4 of them exceeding moderate flood.

events.narrative: A weather station measured 2.92 inches daily rainfall north of Douglas.
A weather station west of Douglas measured a daily rain total of 3.64 inches.

The Skokomish River went above flood stage December 31st, 2020 and stayed above flood stage until January 7, closing roads and cutting off access to the valley. I was above moderate flood at times everyday from January 2nd and the 6th. Urban and small stream flooding occurred as well.
Highway 19 north of the railroad bridge was temporarily closed due to flooding from heavy rain of 5-8 inches in a short period of time.
Heavy rain caused flooding on the Ouachita River at Camden through the first half of January.
Water around 6 inches deep reached the rims of tires near Highway 22 and Cherry Street as well as Bob Little Road due to heavy rainfall of a few inches in a short period of time.
